description:
Turn free text into the occupation and field-of-research codes the speaker-expertise filters take. Call it first whenever a question restricts who is speaking by occupation, profession, credentials or industry ("doctors", "medical professionals", "economists", "people in finance", "lawyers") — the filters, not search wording, decide who speaks — and again when a filter returns `unresolved_reference`, then retry with the code. Codes are SOC 2018 occupations (with their ISCO-08 equivalents) and ANZSRC 2020 fields of research. 'cardiologist' finds SOC 29-1212 Cardiologists; 'finance' finds the finance fields. Each code comes back with its slug, level, parent and the parameters that accept it: `occupation`/`field` on `particle_podcast_list_guests` and `particle_expertise_get`, and `guest_occupation`/`guest_field` on `particle_podcast_find_mentions`, `particle_podcast_list_episodes`, `particle_podcast_search_transcripts`, `particle_podcast_get_episode_timeseries` and `particle_podcast_resolve`. Pass `parent` to walk the hierarchy one level down (a major group's occupations, a division's groups); a broad code filters everything below it.

Not for people or companies — use `particle_person_resolve`, `particle_company_resolve` or `particle_entity_resolve`. Not the topic taxonomy either: `particle_topic_browse` classifies what episodes are about, these codes classify what speakers know.

output_format.description: Output serialization. 'markdown' (default) returns the LLM-facing rendering. 'json' returns the structured payload as JSON text — use only for programmatic chaining where exact field extraction matters; the JSON shape is larger and noisier for an LLM to read.

parent.description: A code, slug or title whose children to list (e.g. '29-0000' for the healthcare occupations, or '38' for economics). With query, searches only below it.

query.description: Free text naming an occupation or a field of research (e.g. 'cardiologist', 'financial analyst', 'constitutional law'). Singular or plural; words match by prefix. Omit with parent to list that code's children, or omit both to list the top level.

standard.description: Which codes to search: 'occupation' (SOC 2018, with ISCO-08 equivalents), 'field' (ANZSRC 2020 fields of research), or 'any' (default) for both.

name: particle_expertise_resolve
